title: Chief Academic Officer
shortSummary: Academic strategy, curriculum integrity & educational quality
about: The Chief Academic Officer (CAO) serves as the senior academic leader of The Open Economics Project, responsible for safeguarding the intellectual integrity and educational quality of the organization's learning resources.

OEP develops economics education across multiple academic pathways, including AP, IB, and A-Level curricula. Maintaining consistency, rigor, and accuracy across these resources requires more than creating content. It requires academic judgment, structured review processes, clear editorial standards, and a long-term commitment to instructional quality.
The CAO will lead this work, helping establish an academic foundation that can support OEP as its publications, assessments, and educational programs expand.
This is a strategic and hands-on leadership position. The successful applicant will be expected to establish standards, coordinate contributors, and personally review important academic work.
mandate: To develop and maintain an academically rigorous, consistent, and reliable ecosystem of economics learning materials that students and educators can confidently use.

responsibilities.heading: Academic Governance and Quality Assurance
items: Develop academic review standards for original lessons, textbooks, question banks, and assessments.
Establish procedures for identifying, reviewing, correcting, and documenting academic errors.
Ensure instructional materials appropriately reflect accepted economic principles and distinguish between competing economic interpretations where relevant.
Maintain consistency in terminology, explanations, diagrams, and academic expectations across resources.

responsibilities.heading: Curriculum Development
items: Coordinate the academic direction of AP Microeconomics, AP Macroeconomics, IB Economics, and A-Level Economics resources.
Identify curriculum gaps and prioritize new academic content.
Develop expectations for assessment difficulty, question construction, explanations, and model answers.
Ensure curriculum-specific requirements are accurately represented without implying affiliation with examination boards.

responsibilities.heading: Academic Team Leadership
items: Coordinate academic contributors, writers, editors, and subject reviewers.
Assign review responsibilities and maintain clear editorial workflows.
Provide constructive feedback and support the development of contributor expertise.
Collaborate with organizational leadership on academic recruitment and contributor standards.

responsibilities.heading: Educational Evaluation
items: Help design comparable assessment questions that can support evaluation of learner understanding.
Review educational feedback and available performance information to recommend improvements.
Support responsible reporting of educational outcomes without overstating the evidence.

candidateProfile: We are seeking someone who demonstrates strong economics knowledge, intellectual discipline, excellent written communication, and sound academic judgment.
Applicants should be capable of explaining complex economic concepts clearly and identifying inaccuracies or weaknesses in instructional materials.

Familiarity with at least one major secondary-level economics curriculum is important. Experience with multiple curricula, tutoring, teaching, educational publishing, or academic review is particularly valuable.
Prior executive experience is not required. Demonstrated competence, accountability, and initiative matter more than an existing leadership title.
roadmapSteps: Review OEP's current academic content structure and identify priority gaps.
Establish a written academic quality-assurance and editorial review framework.
Develop standardized expectations for reviewing lessons and assessments.
Coordinate the academic review of one priority learning unit.
Submit a concise academic development roadmap for the following quarter.
expectations: The CAO will work closely with OEP's executive leadership and relevant academic and technology contributors.
The position requires regular progress communication, timely responses to academic review requests, and an ability to make decisions transparently.

Academic leadership responsibilities do not automatically include unilateral authority to publish materials, enter agreements, or make financial commitments. Final authority will follow OEP's internal governance arrangements.
whyItMatters: Educational reach means little without educational quality. The Chief Academic Officer will help ensure that as OEP reaches more learners, the rigor and reliability of its resources remain central to the organization.
applicationPrep: Applicants should be prepared to describe their economics background, relevant academic experience, approach to quality assurance, and availability. Selected candidates may be invited to complete a short academic-review exercise and interview.

title: Chief Events Officer
expectedCommitment: 2.5–4 hours per week, with event-specific flexibility
about: The Chief Events Officer (CEvO) leads the planning, development, and execution of The Open Economics Project's educational events, competitions, and community-based programs.

OEP's mission is pursued not only through digital learning materials, but also through opportunities for students and communities to engage with economics through writing, discussion, collaboration, and practical learning experiences.
These initiatives require careful administration, clear procedures, reliable coordination, and consistent participant experiences.

The CEvO will oversee the operational structure that makes such programs possible, ensuring that events are well-organized, educationally purposeful, accessible, and capable of being repeated and improved.
This is not simply an event-promotion position. It is a leadership role responsible for translating educational program ideas into successfully delivered initiatives.
mandate: To establish a reliable, scalable framework for OEP's academic competitions, workshops, and educational events, ensuring that each initiative is professionally managed and consistent with the organization's mission.

responsibilities.heading: Event Strategy and Planning
items: Develop and maintain an organizational calendar for competitions, workshops, and educational events.
Establish program objectives, timelines, responsibilities, and delivery milestones.
Create reusable planning templates and event operating procedures.
Coordinate event priorities with OEP's broader organizational strategy.

responsibilities.heading: Academic Competitions
items: Oversee operational planning for essay competitions and other academic initiatives.
Coordinate registration, submission timelines, participant communications, and results announcements.
Organize judging workflows and support the administration of awards and recognition.
Work with academic leadership to maintain fair and consistent evaluation procedures.

responsibilities.heading: Workshops and Community Programs
items: Coordinate virtual and in-person workshops with ambassadors, facilitators, and institutional partners.
Develop event preparation and delivery procedures.
Help identify appropriate facilitators, educational materials, and program formats.
Ensure responsibilities for participant safety, accessibility, and supervision are appropriately assigned.

responsibilities.heading: Program Evaluation
items: Maintain reliable records of event participation and completion.
Collect appropriate feedback from participants and organizers.
Document operational challenges and recommend improvements.
Support OEP's quarterly impact reporting through verifiable program information.

candidateProfile: Applicants should demonstrate strong organizational ability, communication skills, dependable follow-through, and the capacity to coordinate people across different schedules.
Experience planning school programs, academic competitions, conferences, workshops, nonprofit initiatives, or community events is valuable.
Candidates should be comfortable maintaining schedules, delegating responsibilities, solving operational problems, and communicating professionally with external participants.
The ability to remain organized under changing circumstances is particularly important.
roadmapSteps: Review existing and proposed OEP events and competitions.
Develop a six-month event and program calendar.
Create standardized event planning, registration, and evaluation templates.
Define responsibilities for facilitators, judges, and event volunteers.
Produce a delivery plan for one priority event or academic initiative.
expectations: The CEvO will coordinate with executive leadership, the Chief Academic Officer, outreach personnel, ambassadors, and workshop facilitators.
The role requires proactive planning, regular reporting, and advance communication when timelines or deliverables are at risk.

Events involving minors must follow applicable safeguarding procedures. The CEvO is responsible for ensuring that such requirements are incorporated into planning, but is not automatically authorized to act independently of OEP's safeguarding or fiscal-sponsor arrangements.
whyItMatters: A successful educational program is not defined merely by attendance. It must be organized with purpose, administered responsibly, and designed to create a meaningful learning experience. The Chief Events Officer will help OEP deliver that standard consistently.
applicationPrep: Applicants should be prepared to discuss event-management experience, organizational methods, team coordination, and how they would plan an educational initiative from inception through evaluation.

title: Director of Partnerships & Outreach
shortSummary: Institutional relationships, school & NGO outreach & adoption
about: The Director of Partnerships & Outreach is responsible for helping The Open Economics Project establish meaningful relationships with schools, libraries, nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, and community partners.
OEP's educational mission depends not only on producing valuable resources but also on connecting those resources with institutions and communities that can put them to use.

The Director will play an important role in identifying opportunities for collaboration, building institutional relationships, and coordinating initiatives that connect OEP's educational resources with learners beyond its digital platform.
This role requires professional communication, strong initiative, organized relationship management, and the ability to turn introductory conversations into practical collaborations.
mandate: To develop a sustainable network of institutional relationships that supports the distribution, adoption, and community-level use of OEP's educational resources and programs.

responsibilities.heading: Institutional Relationship Development
items: Identify prospective school, library, NGO, and educational partners.
Research institutional needs and assess alignment with OEP's mission.
Prepare personalized outreach communications and introductory materials.
Maintain professional correspondence with prospective and existing partners.

responsibilities.heading: Partnership Coordination
items: Help develop proposals for educational collaborations, resource distribution, and community programming.
Coordinate relevant internal teams during partnership discussions.
Maintain records of partner contacts, discussions, follow-ups, and commitments.
Support the implementation of approved partnership initiatives.

responsibilities.heading: Outreach Strategy
items: Recommend geographic or institutional priorities based on educational need and organizational capacity.
Develop repeatable outreach procedures and communications templates.
Coordinate with student ambassadors to identify credible local opportunities.
Support institutional engagement around educational publications and programs.

responsibilities.heading: Reporting and Accountability
items: Maintain an organized record of outreach activities and partnership development.
Distinguish initial contacts from active institutional collaborations.
Document completed activities and measurable outcomes.
Contribute verified information to OEP's quarterly impact reports.

candidateProfile: Strong written communication, professional judgment, reliability, and the ability to represent an organization credibly are essential.
Experience in student leadership, outreach, community organizations, partnership development, or nonprofit initiatives is desirable.
Applicants should be comfortable conducting independent research, composing formal correspondence, maintaining organized records, and following through on commitments.
roadmapSteps: Review OEP's existing partnership materials and outreach priorities.
Establish a structured partner-prospect database and follow-up process.
Develop professional templates for institutional outreach.
Identify a focused group of credible prospective partners.
Advance suitable partnership discussions and document their status.
expectations: This position works closely with the Chief Development Officer and other relevant organizational leaders.

The Director may initiate approved outreach and coordinate discussions within their assigned responsibilities. They may not independently promise financial support, sign binding agreements, or represent an arrangement as formally approved without authorization.
Partnership success should be judged by relationship quality and documented outcomes—not the number of emails sent.
whyItMatters: The strength of an educational initiative is partly determined by whether its resources reach institutions and communities capable of using them meaningfully. This role connects OEP's work with those opportunities.
applicationPrep: Applicants should demonstrate strong communication, an understanding of institutional outreach, and the ability to build relationships systematically.

title: Director of Brand & Communications
shortSummary: Brand identity, creative direction & communications strategy
about: The Director of Brand & Communications leads the visual identity, creative direction, and public-facing communications of The Open Economics Project.
OEP communicates with students, educators, institutional partners, volunteers, and supporters across diverse educational and geographic contexts.
Maintaining credibility requires a recognizable visual identity, consistent institutional messaging, and communications that reflect the seriousness of the organization's educational mission.
The Director will oversee how OEP presents its work, ensuring that communications are visually coherent, professionally written, and appropriate for their intended audiences.
The role combines creative strategy with practical design and communications responsibilities.
mandate: To establish and maintain a distinctive, credible, and consistent organizational identity across OEP's digital presence, educational publications, campaigns, and institutional communications.

responsibilities.heading: Brand Strategy and Visual Identity
items: Develop and maintain OEP's visual identity standards.
Establish guidance for typography, color, imagery, layouts, and logo usage.
Ensure consistency across the website, social media, publications, and public materials.
Review design output for clarity, visual quality, and accessibility.

responsibilities.heading: Creative Direction and Design
items: Oversee graphic design for educational campaigns, competitions, and outreach initiatives.
Develop visual concepts for program announcements and organizational milestones.
Support publication covers, promotional graphics, and institutional presentation materials.
Coordinate additional creative contributors when appropriate.

responsibilities.heading: Communications and Marketing
items: Develop coordinated communications campaigns for OEP initiatives.
Help manage editorial calendars for social media and public announcements.
Maintain consistent messaging across public channels.
Collaborate with events and partnership teams on program promotion.

responsibilities.heading: Institutional Reputation
items: Review communications for professionalism, accuracy, and consistency with OEP's mission.
Help communicate organizational developments without overstating achievements.
Support the presentation of verified impact reporting and public educational resources.

candidateProfile: Applicants should possess strong visual communication skills, excellent writing ability, and a clear understanding of brand consistency.
Experience with Figma, Adobe Creative Cloud, Canva, or comparable design software is valuable.
Candidates should be able to demonstrate completed work through a portfolio, campaign samples, publication designs, or other relevant examples.
Experience managing a brand or communications calendar is preferred, but demonstrated creative quality and reliability are more important than formal titles.
roadmapSteps: Conduct a visual and communications audit of OEP's public channels.
Produce a concise institutional brand guide.
Establish reusable templates for common communication needs.
Develop a realistic communications calendar.
Lead the creative execution of one approved organizational campaign.
expectations: The Director will coordinate with the Chief Development Officer, events leadership, and relevant publication teams.
The position requires both strategic judgment and willingness to contribute hands-on design work where necessary.
Significant public statements, claims about impact, fundraising communications, and changes to official branding must follow OEP's designated approval procedures.
whyItMatters: An organization's public identity should reflect the quality and seriousness of its underlying work. This role is responsible for ensuring that OEP communicates with the same care it applies to education.
applicationPrep: Applicants should be prepared to share examples of their creative work, discuss their design process, and explain how they would strengthen a mission-driven organization's communications.

title: Director of Global Content & Localization
about: The Director of Global Content & Localization will lead efforts to make The Open Economics Project's educational resources usable across languages, regions, and educational contexts.

Translating educational content requires more than reproducing words in another language. Economic terminology, institutional examples, diagrams, assessment expectations, and pedagogical meaning must all be preserved with care.

As OEP expands its international educational resources, it requires a structured approach to translation, editorial review, publication standards, and the responsible adaptation of materials for different audiences.
The Director will help establish this infrastructure and coordinate the contributors necessary to sustain it.
mandate: To build a reliable multilingual educational publishing process that enables OEP's resources to reach additional audiences without compromising academic accuracy or instructional quality.

responsibilities.heading: Localization Strategy
items: Identify potential priority languages and regions for educational localization.
Assess translation needs based on educational demand, contributor capacity, and program priorities.
Establish a realistic translation and publication roadmap.
Coordinate localization priorities with academic and organizational leadership.

responsibilities.heading: Translation and Editorial Standards
items: Develop consistent standards for economic terminology and translated instructional content.
Establish review workflows involving language proficiency and academic accuracy.
Identify conceptual or contextual differences that require careful adaptation.
Maintain consistency between original and translated educational resources.

responsibilities.heading: Contributor Coordination
items: Recruit or coordinate translators and multilingual reviewers as authorized.
Assign translation projects with clear scopes and deadlines.
Maintain translation progress records and version histories.
Support contributors with terminology guidance and editorial feedback.

responsibilities.heading: Publication and Rights Management
items: Ensure translations retain required attribution and licensing information.
Document substantive adaptations and changes.
Coordinate review of translated materials before publication.
Work with publication and academic teams to maintain updated editions.

candidateProfile: Applicants should demonstrate excellent English communication and strong proficiency in at least one additional language.
Experience in translation, editorial work, multilingual publishing, or localization is especially valuable.
Candidates should possess an appreciation for academic precision and ideally have familiarity with economics terminology.
Previous experience coordinating contributors or maintaining multilingual resources is preferred.
roadmapSteps: Review OEP's available educational content and translation readiness.
Recommend priority languages and initial resource candidates.
Develop a multilingual editorial and terminology framework.
Establish a translation-review and version-control process.
Coordinate a pilot translation and academic review of a manageable resource.
expectations: This position collaborates with the Chief Academic Officer and other relevant content and publication teams.
The Director is responsible for managing the localization process, not personally translating every language in which OEP may eventually publish.
Translated materials must receive appropriate rights and academic review before being released as official OEP publications.
whyItMatters: Knowledge cannot serve a truly international audience if the means of understanding it remain confined to one language or educational context. This role helps make global publication both practical and academically responsible.
applicationPrep: Applicants should identify their language proficiencies, relevant translation or publishing experience, familiarity with educational content, and approach to ensuring accuracy across languages.

title: Student Ambassador
shortSummary: Local relationships, school outreach & community initiatives
expectedCommitment: 1–2 hours per week, depending on initiatives
about: The Student Ambassador Program provides students with an opportunity to represent The Open Economics Project's educational mission within their schools and communities.
Ambassadors serve as local points of connection between OEP and the students, educators, and institutions that may benefit from its resources.
The program emphasizes initiative, responsible leadership, and meaningful community engagement rather than simply promoting an organization's name.
Ambassadors are encouraged to identify genuine educational needs, develop practical outreach ideas, and contribute to initiatives that make economics learning more available in their communities.
This is an opportunity to build leadership skills while contributing to a broader international educational effort.
mandate: To strengthen local awareness and use of OEP's educational resources and help create opportunities for students to engage with economics within their own communities.

responsibilities.heading: Local Outreach
items: Introduce OEP's educational resources to interested students and educators.
Identify schools, clubs, libraries, or student groups that may benefit from OEP initiatives.
Share approved organizational information and program announcements.

responsibilities.heading: Community Initiatives
items: Propose practical educational activities suited to local needs.
Assist with workshops, discussions, and other approved outreach initiatives.
Collaborate with other ambassadors and program leaders where appropriate.

responsibilities.heading: Community Feedback
items: Share observations about students' educational needs and barriers.
Communicate relevant feedback to OEP's central teams.
Document completed activities and the people or institutions reached, without collecting unnecessary personal information.

responsibilities.heading: Organizational Participation
items: Attend reasonable orientation or coordination sessions.
Maintain professional and respectful conduct.
Communicate progress and seek authorization before making external commitments on OEP's behalf.

candidateProfile: The program is intended for motivated students with an interest in economics, education, or community leadership.
Applicants should demonstrate initiative, reliability, communication skills, and a willingness to contribute.
Previous leadership experience is welcomed but is not a prerequisite.
Students do not need to be economics experts, have extensive extracurricular experience, or represent a particular type of educational institution.
roadmapSteps: Complete the ambassador onboarding process.
Become familiar with OEP's resources and organizational guidelines.
Identify a realistic local outreach opportunity.
Submit a concise activity plan for review.
Complete or contribute to an approved outreach activity and document its results.
expectations: Ambassadors are expected to remain reasonably active and maintain communication with their designated program contacts.
OEP values the quality of contributions and local community benefit over superficial activity counts or social media engagement.
Ambassadors do not independently represent OEP in contractual, financial, or official institutional matters without approval.
Additional participation or parental authorization requirements may apply to minors and to particular activities.
whyItMatters: OEP's educational mission cannot be carried by a website alone. Student Ambassadors help translate a global educational purpose into meaningful activity within local communities.
applicationPrep: Applicants should be prepared to describe their educational interests, motivation, community context, and one realistic idea for contributing to OEP's mission.

title: Workshop Facilitator
shortSummary: Guided discussion, explanatory sessions & practical learning
location: Remote or in-person, depending on program
minCommitment: Approximately 1 hour per standard workshop assignment
expectedCommitment: 1–2 hours per standard assignment; longer events may require separate arrangements
about: Workshop Facilitators play a direct role in delivering The Open Economics Project's educational programs.
Through guided discussions, explanatory sessions, practical activities, and community workshops, facilitators help participants engage with economics in structured and approachable ways.
The position requires both subject understanding and the ability to create a respectful, productive learning environment.
Unlike a purely administrative volunteer role, workshop facilitation involves direct responsibility for the quality of participants' learning experiences.
Facilitators may contribute to online workshops, school-based programs, community events, or other approved OEP educational activities.
mandate: To deliver engaging, academically responsible economics learning experiences that encourage participants to ask questions, evaluate ideas, and develop stronger economic understanding.

responsibilities.heading: Session Preparation
items: Review the objectives and instructional materials for assigned workshops.
Prepare a realistic session outline and participant activities.
Coordinate timing, materials, and delivery arrangements with organizers.
Identify content requiring academic clarification before delivery.

responsibilities.heading: Educational Facilitation
items: Explain economic concepts in a clear and accurate manner.
Encourage thoughtful questions and balanced discussion.
Use examples, activities, or exercises to support understanding.
Adjust explanations appropriately for participant knowledge and age.

responsibilities.heading: Participant Experience
items: Maintain an inclusive, respectful learning environment.
Follow relevant safeguarding and conduct standards.
Consider accessibility needs and reasonable adjustments within approved arrangements.
Escalate safety or conduct concerns through designated organizational channels.

responsibilities.heading: Evaluation and Improvement
items: Collect or relay appropriate participant feedback.
Record relevant attendance or delivery information.
Identify instructional challenges and suggest improvements.
Participate in brief post-event reviews when requested.

candidateProfile: Applicants should demonstrate clear communication, comfort speaking to groups, and a reliable understanding of foundational economic concepts.
Experience teaching, tutoring, leading student discussions, conducting workshops, or facilitating community activities is beneficial.
Formal teaching qualifications are not necessarily required, although some programs may require additional experience, supervision, or screening.
Applicants must be willing to follow approved educational materials and program procedures.
roadmapLead: Before leading sessions independently, facilitators should:
roadmapSteps: Complete the relevant orientation.
Review the workshop curriculum and delivery expectations.
Prepare a concise session plan.
Complete any required safeguarding or program-specific screening.
Participate in an initial supported, observed, or otherwise approved workshop.
expectations: Workshop Facilitators collaborate with the Chief Events Officer and designated event or academic leads.
Assignments are offered according to program needs and volunteer availability. No fixed number of workshops is guaranteed.

The stated time commitment is a planning baseline for a standard assignment. Actual preparation, travel, delivery, and follow-up requirements should be communicated and agreed upon before accepting an event.
whyItMatters: Educational resources become more powerful when learners can question, discuss, and apply what they encounter. Workshop Facilitators help create the environment in which that learning can take place.
applicationPrep: Applicants should be prepared to describe their economics background, facilitation experience, communication skills, availability, and approach to engaging learners.
